messages:
mike: Heads up — during this morning's scale run we saw exporter connection timeouts jump and ~5-10% spans not arriving. attaching short log snippet and timings.

mike: logs: `dial tcp 10.0.1.5:4317: i/o timeout` and a LOT of `deadline exceeded` around the same window. spikes coincide with node churn.

mike: current config (simplified):
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/grpc:
    endpoint: telemetry.internal:4317
    timeout: 10s
    retry:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 5s
      max_interval: 30s
      max_elapsed_time: 300s
    headers: {}
  otlp/http:
    endpoint: https://telemetry.internal/v1/traces
    timeout: 15s
```

sara: hmm. 10s dial deadline seems short when backends are cold or when a pod is draining. do we have HTTP fallback enabled in the runtime?

tom: we do, but fallback path currently waits for the gRPC path to error out (so it's basically serial). that explains some of the loss under transient failures.

olivia: two levers: 1) make fallback parallel/hedged (try http after 50ms), 2) adaptive dial timeout based on recent success latency. both risky but worth canarying.

ali: +1 on hedging. also add jitter to the retry backoff — we currently use fixed intervals which cause thundering herd on recovery.

morgan: we should be careful with hedging and semantically-idempotent data. for spans maybe OK, but ensure dedupe on ingest side or use request-id headers.

mike: agree. ingest team already supports idempotency via span IDs, but we'll add a decorator header `x-rw-retry-id` for extra safety.

infra-bot: alert: exporter-error-rate > 5% for 12m (rule: telemetry.exporter.errors.rate)

sara: quick proposal for a canary tuning patch:
```yaml
exporter_tuning:
  dial_timeout: 20s              # increase dial deadline
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    delay_before_secondary: 50ms
    max_attempts: 2
  retry:
    jitter: true
    initial_interval: 300ms
    max_interval: 30s
  fallback:
    mode: parallel_prefer_grpc
    http_priority: low
```

tom: can we also prewarm connections on scaling events? i.e., when we launch new nodes, hit telemetry endpoints from init to populate conn pools. that reduces cold-dial spikes.

olivia: yeah, add a warmup hook in the deployment lifecycle. also adjust http2 keepalive on the client to detect broken backends faster but not too aggressive.

ali: for retries: don't retry non-idempotent operations. for spans it's fine, but ensure backpressure/queue bloat doesn't happen. maybe cap in-flight retries per-host.

mike: action items:
- mike: open PR with the config changes + `x-rw-retry-id` header (I'll do this)
- tom: add a simple prewarm init container to staging and run a 2h soak (assigning to you)
- olivia: coordinate keepalive params with infra (you own testing)
- ali: add jittered backoff implementation review
- morgan: confirm ingest dedupe guarantees and risk doc

morgan: noted. ingest dedupe is probabilistic for duplicates with same trace/span IDs; we'll add deterministic dedupe for the canary period.

sara: rollout plan suggestion: deploy config change to 5% of telemetry clients for 1h, monitor exporter.error_rate, span arrival pct, and end-to-end latency. if stable -> 25% for 2h -> 100%.

tom: also run ablation tests toggling hedging on/off in staging to measure duplicate rate and cost delta. hedging will increase requests ~1.8x in failure cases. need to quantify.

mike: agreed. I'll include the canary policy in the PR description.

ali: small note: ensure the SDK exposes per-tenant overrides behind a feature flag, but default remains centralized. don't want many pod-level knobs for customers.

olivia: UX question — Console: should we surface exporter health and per-tenant retry/backoff profiles? might help SREs debug.

mike: yes, but gated: for GA keep basic metrics (errors, p99 dial, fallback count). advanced tuning UI after we validate defaults.

sara: I'll draft monitoring dashboards: exporter:errors, exporter:hedge_count, exporter:fallback_count, conn_pool_size, dial_latency_p99.

infra-bot: deployment queued: mike/exporter-tuning #2345 -> staging

mike: thanks all. I'll post the PR link when ready and ping for review. :thumbsup:

morgan: good path. keep infra-bot alerts on for the canary window.

tom: 1 more: include a short script to simulate heavy churn (kill 30% pods in 30s) so we can reproduce. I'll add it to the perf repo.

mike: perfect. wrapping up — expect PR in ~2h.
